# Krylov-FSP-SSA vs AdaptiveFSP Comparison
# For reviewer response: demonstrates flux-aware pruning advantages
#
# Tier 1: Oregonator — full quantitative comparison
# Tier 2: Bottleneck — connectivity failure diagnostic
# Tier 3: Robertson — stiffness failure diagnostic

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Tier 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)

    # Run KrylovFSP
    # τ_init=1e-6 is accepted without halving; max_iter=10000 caps at ~t=0.01
    # This demonstrates that KrylovFSP needs ~10x more iterations for partial coverage
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=10000)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=1e-6, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=10000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Oregonator Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Final |S|",
            sol_afsp.state_space_sizes[end], sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes[end]))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Max |S|",
            maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes), maximum(sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Time reached",
            sol_afsp.t[end], sol_kfsp.t[end]))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP rejections", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP total iters", diag_kfsp.total_iters))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean trajectories overlaid
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean trajectories", xlabel="Time", ylabel="Population")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 1], label="X (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="Y (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="Z (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 1], label="X (KrylovFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="Y (KrylovFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="Z (KrylovFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (b) State space size over time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (c) dt/τ over time
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Time step size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1
        dt_afsp = diff(sol_afsp.t)
        plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t[2:end], dt_afsp, label="AdaptiveFSP dt", color=:blue)
    end
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) Marginal distribution at final time
    p4 = plot(title="(d) Marginal P(X) at t_f", xlabel="X", ylabel="Probability")
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        m_afsp = marginal(sol_afsp, length(sol_afsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_afsp.values, m_afsp.probs, label="AdaptiveFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:blue)
    end
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        m_kfsp = marginal(sol_kfsp, length(sol_kfsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_kfsp.values, m_kfsp.probs, label="KrylovFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:red)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Tier 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Failure Diagnostic
# ============================================================================
function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
    bounds = (0, Int(1e11))
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e5), rates; bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP (full, as reference)
    # ε_dt=1e-3 balances fine resolution with completion in reasonable time
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP (reference)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1e-3, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Check if B=1 state was lost in KrylovFSP
    bottleneck_state = CartesianIndex(0, 1, 0)
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        final_states_kfsp = sol_kfsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_kfsp)
        println("  KrylovFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck")
    end

    # Check bottleneck presence in AdaptiveFSP
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        final_states_afsp = sol_afsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck_afsp = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_afsp)
        println("  AdaptiveFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck_afsp")
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Bottleneck Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    t_reached_afsp = sol_afsp.t[end]
    t_reached_kfsp = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", t_reached_afsp, t_reached_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <A>", traj_afsp[end, 1], traj_kfsp[end, 1]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <B>", traj_afsp[end, 2], traj_kfsp[end, 2]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <C>", traj_afsp[end, 3], traj_kfsp[end, 3]))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean of C over time
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean C trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<C>")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Mean of B over time (shows bottleneck loss)
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean B trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<B>")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (c) State space size
    p3 = plot(title="(c) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p3, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) KrylovFSP diagnostics: τ and mass over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) KrylovFSP diagnostics", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Value")
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        iters = 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p4, iters, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="τ", color=:blue, yscale=:log10)
        plot!(twinx(p4), iters, diag_kfsp.mass_log, label="mass", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, ylabel="Mass", legend=:bottomright)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Tier 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic
# ============================================================================
function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    tf = 10.0  # Both methods complete; shows stiffness handling differences
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, tf), rates;
                      bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP (tf=$tf)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=0.01, prob_quantile=0.4, flux_tolerance=1e-9, save_interval=5000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=0.1, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Compute extrapolated completion time
    t_reached = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    if t_reached > 0 && t_kfsp > 0
        extrapolated = t_kfsp * (tf / t_reached)
    else
        extrapolated = Inf
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Robertson Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Total iterations", length(sol_afsp.t)-1, diag_kfsp.total_iters))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", sol_afsp.t[end], t_reached))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15d", "Rejections", "N/A", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Final τ", "N/A", diag_kfsp.τ_log[end]))
    end
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Extrapolated completion (s)", "---", extrapolated))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) τ vs iteration (shows halving cascade)
    p1 = plot(title="(a) τ vs iteration", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p1, 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log), diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Simulated time reached vs wall time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Simulated time vs wall time",
              xlabel="Wall time (s)", ylabel="Simulated time")
    if length(diag_kfsp.walltime_log) > 0
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.walltime_log, diag_kfsp.time_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end
    # Show AdaptiveFSP final point for reference
    scatter!(p2, [t_afsp], [sol_afsp.t[end]], label="AdaptiveFSP (complete)",
             color=:blue, markersize=8, markershape=:star5)

    # (c) Mass conservation over iterations
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Probability mass", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Mass")
    if length(diag_kfsp.mass_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, 1:length(diag_kfsp.mass_log), diag_kfsp.mass_log,
              label="KrylovFSP mass", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (d) State space size over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) State space size", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="|S|")
    if length(diag_kfsp.size_log) > 0
        plot!(p4, 1:length(diag_kfsp.size_log), diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved robertson_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Run all comparisons
# ============================================================================
println("Krylov-FSP-SSA vs AdaptiveFSP Comparison")
println("Output directory: $OUTDIR\n")

res_oreg = run_oregonator_comparison()
res_bottle = run_bottleneck_comparison()
res_robertson = run_robertson_comparison()

println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
println("ALL COMPARISONS COMPLETE")
println("=" ^ 60)
println("Output files in: $OUTDIR")

1024→\paragraph{Oregonator.}
  1025→Table~\ref{tab:comparison_oregonator} and Figure~\ref{fig:oregonator_comparison} compare the two methods on the Oregonator system over $[0, 0.11]$.
  1026→The flux-based adaptive FSP completes the simulation in 41\,s using 28 snapshots with a maximum active set of 1058 states, while the Krylov-FSP-SSA method, using a fixed step $\tau = 10^{-6}$ (the largest step that avoids numerical overflow in the Krylov exponential), reaches only $t = 0.01$ (9\% of the time horizon) after 10{,}000 iterations and 438\,s of wall time, with an active set that grows to 15{,}850 states. The state space explosion (panel~b) arises because the probability-only pruning threshold ($\varepsilon = 10^{-2}$) retains many states with small probability that the flux-based rule would prune, while failing to identify the dynamically essential boundary states. The time step comparison (panel~c) illustrates the core advantage of flux-adaptive stepping: the adaptive FSP adjusts $\Delta t$ over two orders of magnitude ($10^{-6}$ to $10^{-4}$) in response to the instantaneous total flux, whereas the Krylov-FSP-SSA method is locked at $\tau = 10^{-6}$ because larger steps cause mass loss exceeding the tolerance.
  1027→

  1029→\centering
  1030→\caption{Oregonator comparison: flux-based adaptive FSP vs.\ Krylov-FSP-SSA.}
  1031→\label{tab:comparison_oregonator}
  1032→\begin{tabular}{lcc}

  1034→Metric & Adaptive FSP & Krylov-FSP-SSA \\
  1035→\hline
  1036→Wall time (s) & 41 & 438 \\
  1037→Snapshots / Iterations & 28 & 10{,}000 \\
  1038→Time reached & 0.11 (complete) & 0.01 (9\%) \\
  1039→Max $|S|$ & 1{,}058 & 15{,}850 \\
  1040→Final $|S|$ & 1{,}034 & 15{,}850 \\
  1041→Rejections & --- & 0 \\
  1042→\hline
  1043→\end{tabular}
  1044→\end{table}
  1045→

  1047→    \centering

  1049→    \caption{Oregonator: flux-based adaptive FSP (solid blue) vs.\ Krylov-FSP-SSA (dashed red). (a) Mean trajectories: the adaptive FSP completes the full oscillatory dynamics while Krylov-FSP-SSA covers only 9\% of the time horizon. (b) State space size: Krylov-FSP-SSA grows to $\sim$16{,}000 states without flux-based pruning, while the adaptive FSP maintains $<$1{,}100. (c) Time step: the adaptive method adjusts $\Delta t$ by two orders of magnitude; Krylov-FSP-SSA is fixed at $\tau = 10^{-6}$. (d) Marginal distribution $P(X)$ at the final time reached by each method.}
  1050→    \label{fig:oregonator_comparison}

  1053→\paragraph{Bottleneck.}
  1054→Table~\ref{tab:comparison_bottleneck} and Figure~\ref{fig:bottleneck_comparison} compare the methods on the bottleneck system ($A \to B \to B + C$, $k_1 = 10^{-6}$, $k_2 = 0.1$) over $[0, 10^5]$. This system provides the clearest demonstration of connectivity preservation. The flux-based adaptive FSP completes the simulation in 2{,}558\,s, maintaining the bottleneck state $B = 1$ throughout and achieving $\langle C \rangle = 357$ at the final time. The Krylov-FSP-SSA method completes in 0.3\,s (500 iterations) but produces $\langle C \rangle = 18.7$, substantially underestimating the production of species~$C$.
  1055→
  1056→The discrepancy arises because the bottleneck state $(0, 1, c)$ carries very low probability ($\sim 10^{-6}$) at any given time, well below the Krylov-FSP-SSA pruning threshold of $\varepsilon = 10^{-4}$. Without flux protection, this state is pruned, severing the only pathway through which probability can flow from the $A = 1$ initial condition to the $C$-producing reaction $B \to B + C$. The flux-based method protects this state because its outgoing flux ($p(B=1) \times k_2$) is significant relative to the total system flux, despite the low probability. Panel~(c) shows the state space evolution: the adaptive FSP maintains a larger active set to preserve the bottleneck pathway, while Krylov-FSP-SSA operates with a compact but disconnected state space.

Figure~\ref{fig:robertson_comparison} shows the initial $\tau$ halving cascade---from $\tau_{\mathrm{init}} = 0.1$ down to $\sim 10^{-14}$---followed by rapid recovery once the matrix exponential absorbs the fast transient.

## Project overview
Julia package implementing adaptive FSP for stochastic chemical kinetics.
Key methods: `AdaptiveFSP` (FP-FSP), `KrylovFSP` (baseline).
See `src/adaptive_fsp/solve.jl`, `src/adaptive_fsp/krylov_fsp.jl`.

## Comparison plots (examples/comparison.jl)
Three focused failure-mode figures for the paper. See `comparison_plots.md` for details.

### Quick reference
- **Figure 1 Oregonator**: 2-panel (900×350), FP-FSP full + KrylovFSP max_iter=3000
  - (a) |S| vs time  (b) dt vs time log scale

  - FP-FSP: explicit fixed δt=10s loop (`run_fpfsp_bottleneck`), NOT `solve()` interface
  - KrylovFSP: max_iter=200, τ_init=1e3, ε=1e-4
  - (a) ⟨C⟩  (b) ⟨B⟩
- **Figure 3 Robertson**: 1-panel (500×350), KrylovFSP only (τ vs iteration log scale)

### Key bottleneck insight
`AdaptiveFSP` with any large ε_dt finishes the bottleneck in 1 step (dt=tf) and gives ⟨C⟩≈0.
Fix: use explicit fixed-δt loop with `expand!(depth=1)` (deterministic, reproducible).
δt=10s is << 1/k2=10s cutoff. 10000 steps covers tf=1e5s in ~1 minute.

Figure captions updated in `paper/ex_article.tex` to match 2-panel / 1-panel layouts.

- `src/state_space.jl` — added `prune_threshold!` function

## Run command
```
julia --project examples/comparison.jl
```
Expected: < 5 min total. Oregonator ~40s+2min, Bottleneck ~1-2min, Robertson <1s.

Use `Random.seed!(1)` (not `Random.default_rng(1)` which is invalid syntax).

# FP-FSP vs Krylov-FSP-SSA Comparison
# Three focused failure-mode demonstrations:
#
#   Figure 1: Oregonator  — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
#   Figure 2: Bottleneck  — Connectivity Loss
#   Figure 3: Robertson   — τ Halving Cascade
#
# Run: julia --project examples/comparison.jl
# Expected wall time: < 5 min total

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Expokit, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Figure 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    save_interval_afsp = 1000
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run FP-FSP (~40 s)
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=save_interval_afsp,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s, " *
            "max|S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes))")

    # Run KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000: reaches t~0.003, shows explosion, ~2 min)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=1e-6, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=3000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.size_log)
        println("  KrylovFSP: t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp.t[end]; sigdigits=3)), " *
                "max|S|=$(maximum(diag_kfsp.size_log))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): |S| vs simulated time ──────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) State space size", xlabel="Simulated time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes,
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.time_log)
        plot!(p1, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Time step vs simulated time (log scale) ────────────────
    # FP-FSP dt: average per-step dt estimated from snapshot intervals
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Time step", xlabel="Simulated time",
              ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1

res_bottle     = run_bottleneck_comparison()

# FP-FSP vs Krylov-FSP-SSA Comparison
# Three focused failure-mode demonstrations:
#
#   Figure 1: Oregonator  — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
#   Figure 2: Bottleneck  — Connectivity Loss
#   Figure 3: Robertson   — τ Halving Cascade
#
# Run: julia --project examples/comparison.jl
# Expected wall time: < 5 min total

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Figure 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    save_interval_afsp = 1000
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run FP-FSP (~40 s)
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=save_interval_afsp,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s, " *
            "max|S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes))")

    # Run KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000: reaches t~0.003, shows explosion, ~2 min)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=1e-6, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=3000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.size_log)
        println("  KrylovFSP: t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp.t[end]; sigdigits=3)), " *
                "max|S|=$(maximum(diag_kfsp.size_log))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): |S| vs simulated time ──────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) State space size", xlabel="Simulated time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes,
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.time_log)
        plot!(p1, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Time step vs simulated time (log scale) ────────────────
    # FP-FSP dt: average per-step dt estimated from snapshot intervals
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Time step", xlabel="Simulated time",
              ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1
        dt_afsp = diff(sol_afsp.t) ./ save_interval_afsp
        plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t[2:end], dt_afsp,
              label="FP-FSP dt", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    end
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss
# ============================================================================

"""
    run_fpfsp_bottleneck(prob, δt, N_steps, prob_quantile, flux_tol, save_every)

Run FP-FSP on the bottleneck system using a **fixed** time step `δt` and
deterministic `expand!(depth=1)` expansion. This ensures the C-production chain
grows one state per step without SSA randomness, giving reproducible results.

Returns `(t, means)` where `means[i]` is the n_species mean vector at time `t[i]`.
"""
function run_fpfsp_bottleneck(prob::FSPProblem, δt::Float64, N_steps::Int,
                               prob_quantile::Float64, flux_tol::Float64,
                               save_every::Int)
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc    = prob.bc
    u0    = prob.u0
    n_species = length(Tuple(u0))

    sp = StateSpace{CartesianIndex{3}, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, u0, 1.0)

    t_saved    = Float64[0.0]
    means_saved = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    push!(means_saved, Float64[u0[d] for d in 1:n_species])

    for iter in 1:N_steps
        t = iter * δt

        # Deterministic expansion: add all stoichiometric neighbors
        expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=1)

        # Build CME generator and propagate
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)
        p_new = expmv(δt, A, sp.probs)

        # Clamp numerical noise
        @inbounds for i in eachindex(p_new)
            p_new[i] < 0 && (p_new[i] = 0.0)
        end
        sp.probs = p_new

        # Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, prob_quantile; flux_tolerance=flux_tol)
        renormalize!(sp)

        if iter % save_every == 0 || iter == N_steps
            μ = zeros(n_species)
            for (i, s) in enumerate(sp.states)
                for d in 1:n_species
                    μ[d] += s[d] * sp.probs[i]
                end
            end
            push!(t_saved, t)
            push!(means_saved, μ)
        end
    end

    return (t=t_saved, means=means_saved)
end

function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = Float64[1e-6, 1e-1]
    u0    = CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0)
    tf    = 1e5
    prob  = FSPProblem(rn, u0, (0.0, tf), rates; bounds=(0, Int(1e11)))

    # ── FP-FSP: fixed δt=10 s, 10 000 steps (covers full tf=1e5 s) ──────
    # Deterministic expand! grows the C chain one state per step.
    # Flux-aware pruning retains states near the Poisson distribution peak.
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP (fixed δt=10 s, 10 000 steps)...")
    t_afsp_start = time()
    res_afsp = run_fpfsp_bottleneck(prob, 10.0, 10_000, 0.9, 1e-6, 100)
    t_afsp   = time() - t_afsp_start
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(res_afsp.t)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")
    println("  FP-FSP final: ⟨B⟩=$(round(res_afsp.means[end][2]; sigdigits=4)), " *
            "⟨C⟩=$(round(res_afsp.means[end][3]; sigdigits=4))")

    # ── KrylovFSP: probability-threshold pruning severs the C chain ──────
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=200)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=200,
    ))
    t_kfsp   = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if size(traj_kfsp, 1) > 0
        println("  KrylovFSP final: ⟨B⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,2]; sigdigits=4)), " *
                "⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): Mean ⟨C⟩ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean ⟨C⟩", xlabel="Time", ylabel="⟨C⟩")
    plot!(p1, res_afsp.t, [m[3] for m in res_afsp.means],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Mean ⟨B⟩ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean ⟨B⟩", xlabel="Time", ylabel="⟨B⟩")
    plot!(p2, res_afsp.t, [m[2] for m in res_afsp.means],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (res_afsp=res_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 3: Robertson — τ Halving Cascade
# ============================================================================
function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 3: Robertson — τ Halving Cascade")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates  = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    tf     = 10.0
    prob   = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, tf), rates;
                        bounds=bounds)

    # KrylovFSP only: shows τ cascade from 0.1 → ~1e-14 then recovery (~0.3 s)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500, tf=$tf)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=0.1, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, " *
            "$(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, $(round(t_kfsp; digits=2))s")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        println("  τ range: $(minimum(diag_kfsp.τ_log)) to $(maximum(diag_kfsp.τ_log))")
    end

    # ── Single panel: τ vs iteration (log scale) ──────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="τ vs. iteration", xlabel="Iteration",
              ylabel="τ", yscale=:log10)
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p1, 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log), diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    fig = plot(p1; size=(500, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved robertson_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss
# ============================================================================
function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
    u0    = CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0)
    tf    = 1e5
    prob  = FSPProblem(rn, u0, (0.0, tf), rates; bounds=(0, Int(1e11)))

    # ── FP-FSP: flux-aware pruning retains the B=1 bottleneck state ──────
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp    = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")
    println("  FP-FSP final: ⟨B⟩=$(round(traj_afsp[end,2]; sigdigits=4)), " *
            "⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_afsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4))")

    # ── KrylovFSP: probability-threshold pruning severs the bottleneck ───
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp    = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if size(traj_kfsp, 1) > 0
        println("  KrylovFSP final: ⟨B⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,2]; sigdigits=4)), " *
                "⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): Mean ⟨C⟩ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean ⟨C⟩", xlabel="Time", ylabel="⟨C⟩")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Mean ⟨B⟩ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean ⟨B⟩", xlabel="Time", ylabel="⟨B⟩")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# FP-FSP vs Krylov-FSP-SSA Comparison
# Three focused failure-mode demonstrations:
#
#   Figure 1: Oregonator  — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
#   Figure 2: Bottleneck  — Connectivity Loss
#   Figure 3: Robertson   — τ Halving Cascade
#
# Run: julia --project examples/comparison.jl
# Expected wall time: < 5 min total

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Figure 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    save_interval_afsp = 1000
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run FP-FSP (~40 s)
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=save_interval_afsp,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s, " *
            "max|S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes))")

    # Run KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000: reaches t~0.003, shows explosion, ~2 min)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=1e-6, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=3000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.size_log)
        println("  KrylovFSP: t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp.t[end]; sigdigits=3)), " *
                "max|S|=$(maximum(diag_kfsp.size_log))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): |S| vs simulated time ──────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) State space size", xlabel="Simulated time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes,
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.time_log)
        plot!(p1, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Time step vs simulated time (log scale) ────────────────
    # FP-FSP dt: average per-step dt estimated from snapshot intervals
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Time step", xlabel="Simulated time",
              ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1
        dt_afsp = diff(sol_afsp.t) ./ save_interval_afsp
        plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t[2:end], dt_afsp,
              label="FP-FSP dt", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    end
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss
# ============================================================================
function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
    u0    = CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0)
    tf    = 1e5
    prob  = FSPProblem(rn, u0, (0.0, tf), rates; bounds=(0, Int(1e11)))

    # ── FP-FSP: flux-aware pruning retains the B=1 bottleneck state ──────
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp    = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")
    println("  FP-FSP final: ⟨B⟩=$(round(traj_afsp[end,2]; sigdigits=4)), " *
            "⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_afsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4))")

    # ── KrylovFSP: probability-threshold pruning severs the bottleneck ───
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp    = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if size(traj_kfsp, 1) > 0
        println("  KrylovFSP final: ⟨B⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,2]; sigdigits=4)), " *
                "⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): Mean ⟨C⟩ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean ⟨C⟩", xlabel="Time", ylabel="⟨C⟩")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Mean ⟨B⟩ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean ⟨B⟩", xlabel="Time", ylabel="⟨B⟩")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 3: Robertson — τ Halving Cascade
# ============================================================================
function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 3: Robertson — τ Halving Cascade")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates  = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    tf     = 10.0
    prob   = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, tf), rates;
                        bounds=bounds)

# Bottleneck System: A→B, B→B+C
# Demonstrates flux-aware pruning preserving bottleneck states
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst

rn = @reaction_network begin
    k1, A --> B
    k2, B --> B + C
end

rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e5), rates;
                  bounds=(0, Int(1e11)))

# Flux-aware run
sol_flux = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6,
                                   save_interval=1000))
traj_flux = mean_trajectory(sol_flux)

# No-flux run (set flux_tolerance=0 to disable flux protection)
sol_noflux = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.7, flux_tolerance=0.0,
                                     save_interval=1000))
traj_noflux = mean_trajectory(sol_noflux)

println("Flux-aware final:  A=$(traj_flux[end,1]), B=$(traj_flux[end,2]), C=$(traj_flux[end,3])")
println("No-flux final:     A=$(traj_noflux[end,1]), B=$(traj_noflux[end,2]), C=$(traj_noflux[end,3])")
println("Flux snapshots: $(length(sol_flux)), No-flux snapshots: $(length(sol_noflux))")

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control: `dt = ε_dt / total_flux`.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> FSPSolution

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (stoichiometric neighbors).
2. Build the CME generator.
3. Compute adaptive time step from boundary flux.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    while t < tf
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space (legacy SSA-style expansion)
        expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)

        # 2) Build generator from scratch (legacy behavior)
        A, in_flow, out_flow = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)

        # 3) Adaptive time step from total outflux
        out_flux = Vector(-out_flow * sp.probs)
        total_flux = sum(out_flux)
        dt = total_flux > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / total_flux : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability
        sp.probs = expmv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 7) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
end

1→"""
     2→    StateSpace{E, T<:Real}
     3→
     4→Tracks active states, their probabilities, and a stable global ID mapping.
     5→
     6→- `states[i]` is the i-th active state.
     7→- `probs[i]`  is its probability.
     8→- `index[x]`  gives the compact position of state `x` in `states`.
     9→- `global_id[x]` gives the permanent ID assigned when `x` was first added.
    10→- `id_to_state[id]` maps permanent ID back to state (append-only).
    11→- `next_id` is the next global ID to assign.
    12→"""
    13→mutable struct StateSpace{E, T<:Real}
    14→    states::Vector{E}
    15→    probs::Vector{T}
    16→    index::Dict{E,Int}
    17→    global_id::Dict{E,Int}
    18→    id_to_state::Vector{E}
    19→    next_id::Int
    20→end
    21→
    22→function StateSpace{E,T}() where {E,T<:Real}
    23→    StateSpace{E,T}(E[], T[], Dict{E,Int}(), Dict{E,Int}(), E[], 1)
    24→end
    25→
    26→Base.length(sp::StateSpace) = length(sp.states)
    27→
    28→"""
    29→    add_state!(space, state, prob=0.0)
    30→
    31→Add `state` with probability `prob`. No-op if already present. O(1).
    32→"""
    33→function add_state!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, state::E, prob::T=zero(T)) where {E,T}
    34→    haskey(sp.index, state) && return sp
    35→    push!(sp.states, state)
    36→    push!(sp.probs, prob)
    37→    sp.index[state] = length(sp.states)
    38→    if !haskey(sp.global_id, state)
    39→        sp.global_id[state] = sp.next_id
    40→        push!(sp.id_to_state, state)
    41→        sp.next_id += 1
    42→    end
    43→    sp
    44→end
    45→
    46→"""
    47→    remove_states!(space, mask)
    48→
    49→Remove states where `mask[i] == true`. Rebuild compact index.
    50→"""
    51→function remove_states!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, remove_mask::BitVector) where {E,T}
    52→    keep = .!remove_mask
    53→    sp.states = sp.states[keep]
    54→    sp.probs = sp.probs[keep]
    55→    empty!(sp.index)
    56→    for (i, s) in enumerate(sp.states)
    57→        sp.index[s] = i
    58→    end
    59→    sp
    60→end
    61→
    62→"""
    63→    expand!(space, model, bc; depth=1)
    64→
    65→Add stoichiometric neighbors of all current states that satisfy `bc`.
    66→Probabilities of new states are initialized to zero.
    67→"""
    68→function expand!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    69→    for _ in 1:depth
    70→        current = copy(sp.states)
    71→        for x in current
    72→            for ν in model.stoichvecs
    73→                y = x + ν
    74→                if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
    75→                    add_state!(sp, y)
    76→                end
    77→            end
    78→        end
    79→    end
    80→    sp
    81→end
    82→
    83→"""
    84→    expand_ssa!(space, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)
    85→
    86→Legacy SSA-style expansion: for each active state, sample one reaction by
    87→propensity and add the sampled successor if it satisfies `bc`.
    88→"""
    89→function expand_ssa!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    90→    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    91→    n_rxn == 0 && return sp
    92→
    93→    for _ in 1:depth
    94→        current = copy(sp.states)
    95→        for x in current
    96→            props = Vector{Float64}(undef, n_rxn)
    97→            total = 0.0
    98→            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
    99→                α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
   100→                α = max(0.0, α)
   101→                props[k] = α
   102→                total += α
   103→            end
   104→            total <= 0 && continue
   105→
   106→            threshold = rand() * total
   107→            csum = 0.0
   108→            chosen = 0
   109→            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
   110→                csum += props[k]
   111→                if threshold <= csum
   112→                    chosen = k
   113→                    break
   114→                end
   115→            end
   116→            chosen == 0 && continue
   117→
   118→            y = x + model.stoichvecs[chosen]
   119→            if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
   120→                add_state!(sp, y)
   121→            end
   122→        end
   123→    end
   124→    sp
   125→end
   126→
   127→"""
   128→    compress!(space, model, rates, t, prob_quantile; flux_tolerance=1e-6)
   129→
   130→Flux-aware pruning with legacy count-quantile candidate selection.
   131→
   132→Candidates are chosen by state count:
   133→`round(prob_quantile * n_states)` lowest-probability states.
   134→If `flux_tolerance <= 0`, all candidates are pruned.
   135→Returns `(total_flux, n_removed)`.
   136→"""
   137→function compress!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real,
   138→                   prob_quantile::Real; flux_tolerance::Real=1e-6) where {E,T}
   139→    n = length(sp)
   140→    n == 0 && return (zero(T), 0)
   141→
   142→    # Compute flux for each state: p(x) * sum_k a_k(x)
   143→    flux = Vector{T}(undef, n)
   144→    @inbounds for i in 1:n
   145→        w = zero(T)
   146→        for prop in model.propensities
   147→            w += prop(sp.states[i], rates, t)
   148→        end
   149→        flux[i] = sp.probs[i] * w
   150→    end
   151→    total_flux = sum(flux)
   152→    flux_threshold = total_flux * flux_tolerance
   153→
   154→    idx = sortperm(sp.probs)
   155→    n_remove = round(Int, clamp(prob_quantile, 0, 1) * n)
   156→    candidates = n_remove > 0 ? idx[1:min(n_remove, n)] : Int[]
   157→
   158→    remove_mask = falses(n)
   159→    n_removed = 0
   160→    if flux_tolerance <= 0
   161→        for i in candidates
   162→            remove_mask[i] = true
   163→            n_removed += 1
   164→        end
   165→    else
   166→        for i in candidates
   167→            if flux[i] < flux_threshold
   168→                remove_mask[i] = true
   169→                n_removed += 1
   170→            end
   171→        end
   172→    end
   173→
   174→    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
   175→    (total_flux, n_removed)
   176→end
   177→
   178→"""
   179→    prune_threshold!(space, threshold; max_probs=nothing)
   180→
   181→Simple threshold-based pruning: remove states whose probability (or lookback-window
   182→max probability, if `max_probs` is provided) is below `threshold`.
   183→Returns the number of states removed.
   184→"""
   185→function prune_threshold!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, threshold::Real;
   186→                          max_probs::Union{Nothing, Dict{E,<:Real}}=nothing) where {E,T}
   187→    n = length(sp)
   188→    n == 0 && return 0
   189→    remove_mask = falses(n)
   190→    n_removed = 0
   191→    for i in 1:n
   192→        p = max_probs !== nothing ? get(max_probs, sp.states[i], sp.probs[i]) : sp.probs[i]
   193→        if p < threshold
   194→            remove_mask[i] = true
   195→            n_removed += 1
   196→        end
   197→    end
   198→    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
   199→    n_removed
   200→end
   201→
   202→"""
   203→    renormalize!(space)
   204→
   205→Scale probabilities so they sum to 1. Returns the sum before normalization.
   206→"""

"""
    StateSpace{E, T<:Real}

Tracks active states, their probabilities, and a stable global ID mapping.

- `states[i]` is the i-th active state.
- `probs[i]`  is its probability.
- `index[x]`  gives the compact position of state `x` in `states`.
- `global_id[x]` gives the permanent ID assigned when `x` was first added.
- `id_to_state[id]` maps permanent ID back to state (append-only).
- `next_id` is the next global ID to assign.
"""
mutable struct StateSpace{E, T<:Real}
    states::Vector{E}
    probs::Vector{T}
    index::Dict{E,Int}
    global_id::Dict{E,Int}
    id_to_state::Vector{E}
    next_id::Int
end

function StateSpace{E,T}() where {E,T<:Real}
    StateSpace{E,T}(E[], T[], Dict{E,Int}(), Dict{E,Int}(), E[], 1)
end

Base.length(sp::StateSpace) = length(sp.states)

"""
    add_state!(space, state, prob=0.0)

Add `state` with probability `prob`. No-op if already present. O(1).
"""
function add_state!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, state::E, prob::T=zero(T)) where {E,T}
    haskey(sp.index, state) && return sp
    push!(sp.states, state)
    push!(sp.probs, prob)
    sp.index[state] = length(sp.states)
    if !haskey(sp.global_id, state)
        sp.global_id[state] = sp.next_id
        push!(sp.id_to_state, state)
        sp.next_id += 1
    end
    sp
end

"""
    remove_states!(space, mask)

Remove states where `mask[i] == true`. Rebuild compact index.
"""
function remove_states!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, remove_mask::BitVector) where {E,T}
    keep = .!remove_mask
    sp.states = sp.states[keep]
    sp.probs = sp.probs[keep]
    empty!(sp.index)
    for (i, s) in enumerate(sp.states)
        sp.index[s] = i
    end
    sp
end

"""
    expand!(space, model, bc; depth=1)

Add stoichiometric neighbors of all current states that satisfy `bc`.
Probabilities of new states are initialized to zero.
"""
function expand!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            for ν in model.stoichvecs
                y = x + ν
                if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                    add_state!(sp, y)
                end
            end
        end
    end
    sp
end

"""
    expand_ssa!(space, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

Legacy SSA-style expansion: for each active state, sample one reaction by
propensity and add the sampled successor if it satisfies `bc`.
"""
function expand_ssa!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    n_rxn == 0 && return sp

    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            props = Vector{Float64}(undef, n_rxn)
            total = 0.0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                α = max(0.0, α)
                props[k] = α
                total += α
            end
            total <= 0 && continue

            threshold = rand() * total
            csum = 0.0
            chosen = 0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                csum += props[k]
                if threshold <= csum
                    chosen = k
                    break
                end
            end
            chosen == 0 && continue

            y = x + model.stoichvecs[chosen]
            if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                add_state!(sp, y)
            end
        end
    end
    sp
end

"""
    compress!(space, model, rates, t, prob_quantile; flux_tolerance=1e-6)

Flux-aware pruning with legacy count-quantile candidate selection.

Candidates are chosen by state count:
`round(prob_quantile * n_states)` lowest-probability states.
If `flux_tolerance <= 0`, all candidates are pruned.
Returns `(total_flux, n_removed)`.
"""
function compress!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real,
                   prob_quantile::Real; flux_tolerance::Real=1e-6) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return (zero(T), 0)

    # Compute flux for each state: p(x) * sum_k a_k(x)
    flux = Vector{T}(undef, n)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        w = zero(T)
        for prop in model.propensities
            w += prop(sp.states[i], rates, t)
        end
        flux[i] = sp.probs[i] * w
    end
    total_flux = sum(flux)
    flux_threshold = total_flux * flux_tolerance

    idx = sortperm(sp.probs)
    n_remove = round(Int, clamp(prob_quantile, 0, 1) * n)
    candidates = n_remove > 0 ? idx[1:min(n_remove, n)] : Int[]

    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    if flux_tolerance <= 0
        for i in candidates
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    else
        for i in candidates
            if flux[i] < flux_threshold
                remove_mask[i] = true
                n_removed += 1
            end
        end
    end

    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    (total_flux, n_removed)
end

"""
    prune_threshold!(space, threshold; max_probs=nothing)

Simple threshold-based pruning: remove states whose probability (or lookback-window
max probability, if `max_probs` is provided) is below `threshold`.
Returns the number of states removed.
"""
function prune_threshold!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, threshold::Real;
                          max_probs::Union{Nothing, Dict{E,<:Real}}=nothing) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return 0
    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    for i in 1:n
        p = max_probs !== nothing ? get(max_probs, sp.states[i], sp.probs[i]) : sp.probs[i]
        if p < threshold
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    end
    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    n_removed
end

"""
    renormalize!(space)

Scale probabilities so they sum to 1. Returns the sum before normalization.
"""
function renormalize!(sp::StateSpace)
    s = sum(sp.probs)
    if s > 0
        sp.probs ./= s
    end
    s
end

"""
    get_global_ids(space) -> Vector{Int}

Return the global IDs of the current active states (in compact order).
"""
function get_global_ids(sp::StateSpace)
    [sp.global_id[s] for s in sp.states]
end

"""
    build_generator(space, model, rates, t) -> (A, in_flow, out_flow)

Build the CME generator matrix from scratch in CSC-friendly COO format.

For each column j (state x_j), iterate over reactions k with stoich vector ν_k:
  - Off-diagonal: A[i,j] += a_k(x_j) where x_j + ν_k = x_i ∈ active set
  - Diagonal:     A[j,j]  = -sum of off-diagonal column entries

Returns `(A, in_flow, out_flow)` where `A = in_flow + out_flow`,
`out_flow = diag(A)` (negative), `in_flow = A - out_flow` (non-negative).
"""
function build_generator(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return (spzeros(T, 0, 0), spzeros(T, 0, 0), spzeros(T, 0, 0))

    # Pre-estimate nnz: at most n_reactions off-diagonal entries per column + 1 diagonal
    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    sizehint = n * (n_rxn + 1)
    I = Vector{Int}(); J = Vector{Int}(); V = Vector{T}()
    sizehint!(I, sizehint); sizehint!(J, sizehint); sizehint!(V, sizehint)

    @inbounds for j in 1:n
        x = sp.states[j]
        col_sum = zero(T)

        for k in 1:n_rxn
            y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
            i = get(sp.index, y, 0)
            if i != 0
                α = convert(T, model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                if α > 0
                    push!(I, i); push!(J, j); push!(V, α)
                    col_sum += α
                end
            end
        end

        if col_sum > 0
            push!(I, j); push!(J, j); push!(V, -col_sum)
        end
    end

    A = sparse(I, J, V, n, n)
    out_flow = spdiagm(0 => diag(A))
    in_flow = A - out_flow
    (A, in_flow, out_flow)
end

"""
    reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old) -> (A, in_flow, out_flow)

Incremental rebuild: reuse columns from `A_old` for states that were present in the
previous step (matched via global IDs). Build new columns from scratch.

Falls back to `build_generator` if overlap is below 30%.
"""
function reconstruct_generator(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real,
                               A_old::SparseMatrixCSC, gids_old::Vector{Int}) where {E,T}
    n_new = length(sp)
    n_new == 0 && return build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)

    gids_new = get_global_ids(sp)

    # Map old global ID → old column index
    old_gid_to_col = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for (col, gid) in enumerate(gids_old)
        old_gid_to_col[gid] = col
    end

    # Count retained columns
    n_retained = count(gid -> haskey(old_gid_to_col, gid), gids_new)
    if n_retained < 0.3 * n_new
        return build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)
    end

    # Build new-row-index lookup for all active states (by global ID)
    gid_to_new_row = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for (row, gid) in enumerate(gids_new)
        gid_to_new_row[gid] = row
    end

    # Old global ID → old row index
    old_gid_to_row = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for (row, gid) in enumerate(gids_old)
        old_gid_to_row[gid] = row
    end

    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    sizehint_n = n_new * (n_rxn + 1)
    I = Vector{Int}(); J = Vector{Int}(); V = Vector{T}()
    sizehint!(I, sizehint_n); sizehint!(J, sizehint_n); sizehint!(V, sizehint_n)

    @inbounds for (j_new, gid) in enumerate(gids_new)
        old_col = get(old_gid_to_col, gid, 0)

        if old_col != 0
            # Retained column: copy old off-diagonal entries + add new neighbors
            x = sp.states[j_new]
            col_sum = zero(T)

            # Collect old off-diagonal targets (by new row index) for dedup
            old_targets = Set{Int}()
            for idx in nzrange(A_old, old_col)
                old_row = A_old.rowval[idx]
                old_row == old_col && continue  # skip diagonal
                val = A_old.nzval[idx]
                old_row_gid = gids_old[old_row]
                new_row = get(gid_to_new_row, old_row_gid, 0)
                if new_row != 0
                    push!(I, new_row); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, val)
                    col_sum += val
                    push!(old_targets, new_row)
                end
            end

            # Check for NEW neighbors not in old state space
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                i_new = get(sp.index, y, 0)
                if i_new != 0 && i_new != j_new && !(i_new in old_targets)
                    # This neighbor is new — compute propensity
                    α = convert(T, model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                    if α > 0
                        push!(I, i_new); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, α)
                        col_sum += α
                    end
                end
            end

            if col_sum > 0
                push!(I, j_new); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, -col_sum)
            end
        else
            # New column: build from scratch
            x = sp.states[j_new]
            col_sum = zero(T)
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                i_new = get(sp.index, y, 0)
                if i_new != 0
                    α = convert(T, model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                    if α > 0
                        push!(I, i_new); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, α)
                        col_sum += α
                    end
                end
            end
            if col_sum > 0
                push!(I, j_new); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, -col_sum)
            end
        end
    end

    A = sparse(I, J, V, n_new, n_new)
    out_flow = spdiagm(0 => diag(A))
    in_flow = A - out_flow
    (A, in_flow, out_flow)
end

	# importing local fsp package

	using .local_mod.DiscStochSim
end

# ╔═╡ cb9fa0aa-1588-4647-8b02-69fca1415974
rn = @reaction_network begin
    k₁, A --> B 
	k₂, B --> B + C
end

# ╔═╡ ae7ff050-c76d-4c0d-8c8a-23724f10485a
model = DiscreteStochasticSystem(rn);

# ╔═╡ 85c4ad39-d14a-4e73-bfa3-4a22fef4d537
def_params = begin
	# reaction rates 
	rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
	# boundary 
	bounds = (0, 1e11) #(lower limit, upper limit)
	boundary_condition(x) = RectLatticeBoundaryCondition(x, bounds);
	# time interval and initial values
end

# ╔═╡ e3e0c398-9db0-420a-86b3-65220761028c
function robust_purge1!(
    X::Set{Element}, 
    p::Vector{T}, 
    model::Model,
    rates,
    t,
    prob_quantile::Number;
    flux_tolerance::Number = 1e-9 
) where {Element, T, Model}

    X_vec = collect(X)

    candidate_idxs = DiscStochSim.findLowestValuesPercent_naive(p, prob_quantile)

    flux_vector = zeros(T, length(p))

    for i in eachindex(X_vec)
        current_state = X_vec[i]
        weight = sum(prop(current_state, rates, t) for prop in model.propensities)
        flux_vector[i] = p[i] * weight
    end

    total_flux = sum(flux_vector)

    # Set an adaptive threshold based on the total system flux
    flux_threshold = total_flux * flux_tolerance

    # Filter the candidates based on this adaptive threshold
    final_idxs_to_prune = Set{Int}()
    for idx in candidate_idxs
        if flux_vector[idx] < flux_threshold
            push!(final_idxs_to_prune, idx)
        end
    end

    # 3. Purge the final set of states
    new_p = [p[i] for i in eachindex(p) if i ∉ final_idxs_to_prune]
    states_to_remove = Set(X_vec[collect(final_idxs_to_prune)])

function reconstruct_MasterEquation(
    S_new::Set{E},
    S_old_vec::Vector{E},         
    A_old::SparseMatrixCSC{T,Int}, 
    model, rates, bc::Function, t::Real;
    overlap_threshold::Real=0.3,
) where {E,T}

    # --- Setup ---
    S_new_vec = collect(S_new)
    n_new = length(S_new_vec)
    new_id = Dict{E,Int}(s => i for (i,s) in enumerate(S_new_vec))
    old_id  = Dict{E,Int}(s => i for (i,s) in enumerate(S_old_vec))

    # --- Overlap check (can be kept as a performance heuristic) ---
    n_retained = count(s -> haskey(old_id, s), S_new_vec)
    if n_new == 0 || n_retained / n_new < overlap_threshold

    end
    
    I = Int[]; J = Int[]; V = T[]
    @inbounds for (j_new, x) in enumerate(S_new_vec)
        col_sum = zero(T)
        
        # Build the entire column from scratch based on propensities
        for (k, ν) in enumerate(model.stoichvecs)
            y = x + ν
            # Check if the destination `y` is in our new state space
            i_new = get(new_id, y, 0)
            
            if i_new != 0
                α = model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)
                if α > 0
                    # Allow duplicates for sparse() to sum them up
                    push!(I, i_new); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, α)
                    col_sum += α
                end
            end
        end
        
        # Diagonal = minus the sum of all off-diagonals in this column
        if col_sum > 0
            push!(I, j_new); push!(J, j_new); push!(V, -col_sum)
        end
    end

    A = sparse(I, J, V, n_new, n_new)
    out_flow = spdiagm(0 => diag(A))
    in_flow  = A - out_flow
    
    return A, in_flow, out_flow

		# 4. Initialize p₀
	local U₀ = CartesianIndex(1,0,0)
	local 𝒮₀ = Set([U₀])
	local p₀ = zeros(length(𝒮₀))
	local p₀[FindElement(U₀,𝒮₀)] = 1.0
	# copy initial values

	local 𝒮ₜ = copy(𝒮₀)

	local iter = 1
	local pₜ = p₀
	local δt = 10.0
	global savefreq=[]
	global T =0:δt:1e5
	
	# variables to store simulation observables
	size_𝒮ₜ = Int.(zeros(length(T))) # system sizes
	flux = zeros(length(T))
	flux_tol = zeros(length(T))
	local_ϵ = zeros(length(T))
	sol = []
	
	@progress for (iter, t) ∈ enumerate(T)
		
		# expand state space

		local A, in_flow, out_flow = MasterEquation(𝒮ₜ, 
													 model,
													 rates,
													 boundary_condition, 
													 t)

		pₜ = expmv(δt, A, pₜ)

		if iter%savefreq == 0
			push!(size_𝒮ₜ[iter], length(𝒮ₜ))
    		push!(sol, (𝒮ₜ, pₜ))
			push!(times, )
		end
		
		# purge state space
		𝒮ₜ, pₜ, total_flux = robust_purge1!(𝒮ₜ, 
									pₜ, 
									model,
									rates,
									δt,
									0.9; flux_tolerance=0.000001)
	 	


		local_ϵ[iter] = 1.0 - sum(pₜ)
    	pₜ ./= sum(pₜ)
		#flux[iter] = max(0.0, 1.0 - δt * total_flux)
		pₜ ./= sum(pₜ)		
	end
	global afsp_mean = map(1:length(sol)) do i
		sum(collect.(Tuple.(sol[i][1])) .* sol[i][2])
	end 
	afsp_mean=hcat(afsp_mean...)'
end

"""
    FSPSolution

Stores snapshots from an adaptive FSP solve.

# Fields
- `t::Vector{Float64}`: Time points of saved snapshots.
- `snapshots::Vector{Tuple{Vector{E}, Vector{Float64}}}`: `(states, probs)` at each snapshot.
- `state_space_sizes::Vector{Int}`: State space size at each snapshot.
- `n_species::Int`: Number of species (dimension of CartesianIndex).
"""
struct FSPSolution{E}
    t::Vector{Float64}
    snapshots::Vector{Tuple{Vector{E}, Vector{Float64}}}
    state_space_sizes::Vector{Int}
    n_species::Int
end

Base.length(sol::FSPSolution) = length(sol.t)

"""
    sol[i] -> (states, probs)

Return the i-th snapshot.
"""
Base.getindex(sol::FSPSolution, i::Int) = sol.snapshots[i]

"""
    mean_trajectory(sol) -> Matrix{Float64}

Compute the mean state at each snapshot. Returns an `n_snapshots × n_species` matrix.
"""
function mean_trajectory(sol::FSPSolution)
    ns = sol.n_species
    nt = length(sol)
    result = zeros(nt, ns)
    for i in 1:nt
        states, probs = sol.snapshots[i]
        for (s, p) in zip(states, probs)
            for d in 1:ns
                result[i, d] += s[d] * p
            end
        end
    end
    result
end

"""
    marginal(sol, i, species) -> (values, probs)

Compute the marginal distribution of `species` (1-indexed) at snapshot `i`.
Returns sorted `(values, probs)` vectors.
"""
function marginal(sol::FSPSolution, i::Int, species::Int)
    states, probs = sol.snapshots[i]
    dist = Dict{Int, Float64}()
    for (s, p) in zip(states, probs)
        v = s[species]
        dist[v] = get(dist, v, 0.0) + p
    end
    vals = sort(collect(keys(dist)))
    ps = [dist[v] for v in vals]
    (values=vals, probs=ps)
end

"""
    FSPProblem(rn, u0, tspan, rates; bounds=(0, 50_000))

Defines a Chemical Master Equation problem for the Finite State Projection method.

# Arguments
- `rn::ReactionSystem`: Catalyst reaction network.
- `u0::CartesianIndex`: Initial state.
- `tspan::Tuple{Real,Real}`: Time interval `(t0, tf)`.
- `rates::Vector`: Reaction rate parameters.
- `bounds`: Domain bounds passed to `RectLatticeBoundaryCondition`.
"""
struct FSPProblem{E, T<:Real}
    model::DiscreteStochasticSystem{E}
    u0::E
    tspan::Tuple{T,T}
    rates::Vector{T}
    bc::Function
end

function FSPProblem(rn::ReactionSystem, u0::CartesianIndex, tspan::Tuple,
                    rates::Vector; bounds=(0, 50_000))
    model = DiscreteStochasticSystem(rn)
    T = promote_type(eltype(rates), typeof(tspan[1]), typeof(tspan[2]))
    tspan_T = (T(tspan[1]), T(tspan[2]))
    rates_T = T.(rates)
    bc = x -> RectLatticeBoundaryCondition(x, bounds)
    FSPProblem{CartesianIndex, T}(model, u0, tspan_T, rates_T, bc)
end
